findings.title: Include the identity type in denial-cache keys
findings.body: The denial key includes the parsed UID but omits IdentityType. Accepted subjects anonymous:0 and render:0 therefore share an entry for the same namespace, action, name, and folder. If an anonymous dashboard read is denied, the renderer's subsequent check returns false from this cache without reaching getRendererPermissions, which grants dashboard reads unconditionally. This can break rendering for 30 seconds. Include the full subject or identity type in the key.

findings.title: Encode denial-cache key components unambiguously
findings.body: Joining Name and ParentFolder with an unescaped underscore allows distinct requests to share a denial entry. For the same namespace, user, and action, Name="dash_a", ParentFolder="b" and Name="dash", ParentFolder="a_b" produce identical keys. A denial for the first request consequently rejects the second for 30 seconds, even if the user's permission map explicitly grants access to dashboard "dash". Use escaping, length prefixes, or another unambiguous tuple encoding.

findings.title: Avoid extending denials caused by a stale folder tree
findings.body: Refreshing the permission map does not refresh the folder tree used by checkInheritedPermissions. For example, a user granted dashboard access on ancestor G can be denied a dashboard whose parent C was just created under G: the cached tree lacks C, and the fresh permission query still correctly returns only the grant on G. This line then caches that stale-tree denial for another 30 seconds. A check just before the folder-cache expiry can therefore remain denied well after the tree expires or is refreshed, whereas previously it would recover when the tree expired. Refresh the relevant hierarchy before caching an inherited denial, or avoid extending denials derived from stale hierarchy data.

findings.title: Actually grant access in the explicit-denial cache test
findings.body: The test says it grants dashboard access to prove that the denial cache takes precedence, but the permission value is false. Without the denial-cache shortcut, checkPermission rejects this entry and the empty fake permission store also denies access, so the test still passes. Set the permission to true so removing or bypassing the denial-cache lookup makes the test fail; asserting that the permission store is not queried would also verify the intended shortcut.
